speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs whether he can explain Singapore's vote in favour of the recent United Nations General Assembly resolution of the 10th Emergency Special Session (ESS) on 21 December 2017 on the Status of Jerusalem, which indirectly criticised the US' decision to recognise Jerusalem as the capital of Israel.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our position over the years has been based on the principle of seeking peaceful resolution of conflicts by upholding international law and abiding fully with UN Security Council Resolutions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It has profound religious significance for Muslims, Jews and Christians, and the status of Jerusalem is a very complex and sensitive issue with a very long history, fraught with political and religious dimensions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These special circumstances of Jerusalem have been addressed by numerous UN resolutions, with the most recent instance being the resolution that was voted upon on 21 December 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, an almost identical resolution was considered by the UN Security Council, a week earlier, on 18 December 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: At that UN Security Council session, 14 of the 15 members of the Security Council voted in favour of the resolution, and the United States (US) was the sole member to vote against and ultimately, to cast a veto against the resolution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And that is why the resolution then came to the General Assembly.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We do not take sides in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our objective has always been to support a peaceful resolution to this conflict.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have been a steadfast advocate of a negotiated two-state solution, with Israel and Palestine living side-by-side in peace and security.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It would impede progress towards a just and durable solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our vote on the recent resolution is, therefore, consistent with this policy position.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It has, at its foundation, a key principle of Singapore's foreign policy, which is the promotion of a rules-based global community, governed by the rule of international law and always seeking peaceful resolution of disputes.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is also in this context that Singapore has always strictly abided by all UN Security Council Resolutions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore's position on this issue is well-known and our vote at the various UN resolutions related to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict have been guided by this same principle, regardless of the positions of others.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Although other states, including the bigger powers, may occasionally differ or disagree with certain positions that we take, we maintain a consistent application of this principle and this ability to maintain consistency over the long term has enabled us to be taken seriously and to be regarded as a reliable partner who can play a constructive role in international affairs.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Indeed, Singapore remains a steadfast partner of the US, of Israel and of the Palestinian people.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our longstanding bilateral relations with all countries are strong and multifaceted, and our shared interests far exceed differences.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: At the same time, this gives us access and a strong relationship based on trust with the Palestinians and, indeed, with the Middle East as a whole.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As a small country with a multiracial and multi-religious population, Singapore, of all countries, fully appreciates that tolerance and the peaceful resolution of disputes are vital for social harmony and for our success as a nation and, indeed, for world peace.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We therefore hope that the parties involved will work towards the resumption of direct peace negotiations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This can only be achieved when both sides approach these longstanding sensitive issues in a spirit of good faith and appreciation for each other's beliefs, values, aspirations, hopes and anxieties.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: First, was there a reason Singapore chose to vote in favour of the resolution rather than, say, abstaining because that is clearly taking a position on the matter?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: And second, Singapore has always advocated a two-state solution and a change in status of Jerusalem, I believe, the Minister was implying would make that more difficult.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: What steps has Singapore taken to facilitate the two-state solution, given its strong relationships with both sides?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On the first question, when you are faced with a resolution, there is always a choice – you can vote in favour, you can abstain or you can vote against.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, there is a fourth choice, which is to be absent.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I think Members of this House will know that that is not Singapore's style.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: When we are confronted with a question, we face it head-on and we make what we believe is an appropriate choice that is consistent with our position, policy and our values.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As I explained earlier, the real problem or the catalyst for this current resolution, and I am going to say what I am going say now without naming names and without identifying countries, but what really precipitated this was an announcement.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: An announcement which could be construed as changing the status quo.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is a principled decision because we are actually not taking sides, but not saying one party or the other or its supporters are right or wrong.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are not a key player in the Middle East.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For our approach, I would look at it at two levels.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: First, we do want to be friends with everyone but we want to be not just a fair-weathered friends.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We want to be long-term, reliable and principled friends.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For that kind of relationship to occur, when you have two parties who have been fighting for thousands of years, you can imagine it is a very difficult role to play.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Nevertheless, because both Israelis as well as the Palestinians, and the Arabs and all the other countries in the Middle East know that Singapore does not take sides.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: They know that we do not bend for the sake of pressure or inducements and that we genuinely stand for peace and for development.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Among the various parts of the trip, I think the most significant was when we had a chance to go up to Temple Mount, or the Arabic term, the Al-Haram Al-Sharif, where the Dome of the Rock is and where Al-Aqsa Mosque is.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: At the risk of being longwinded, let me tell you my sentiments, as the Prime Minister and our delegation, including Minister Masagos and Member of Parliament Dr Intan, went along with us.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The first sense I got was the sense of awe.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Whether or not you are religious, if you visit Jerusalem and you go to those sites, you cannot help but feel that this is a special place, a sacred place.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: A place where heaven and earth seems to come to a confluence.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: My second sense was gratitude for being a Singaporean because here we were accompanied by security from both the Israeli and Jordanian sides and they gave us full access.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Minister Masagos even had the chance to pray in the cave beneath the Dome of the Rock.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And they gave us full access to the Al-Aqsa Mosque and we are not Muslims.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But everyone knew we were from Singapore, this is a multi-religious, multiracial group, and we were welcomed and were protected by both parties.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, there was that sense of gratitude, that sense of special access.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: People talk about the Singapore passport being very powerful.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is not really about the passport but the fact that the world welcomes and trusts us.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The third sentiment I felt during that trip was I thought about thousands of lives that had been lost and all the blood that had been shed on that hill, in the name of race, language and religion.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It made me more determined than before to appreciate what we have in Singapore, that when we say we believe in peaceful resolution and we believe in direct, honest negotiations and that we believe in living side by side, even to the point where we need an Ethnic Integration Policy, we are not just describing to the world.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are living a real example of multiracial, multi-religious peace.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: When we say to live side by side in peace and security, we are a working vision, a working example of that future.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And from time to time, we will have to take a different position from friends or supporters but I am confident that they know Singapore, they know Singaporeans well and they know that we do not grandstand, we do not take political postures for the sake of posturing.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But we do so in all sincerity as a reflection of who we are as a multi-religious society and our longstanding friendship, support and advocacy for peace in the Middle East.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That, in a nutshell, is about all that we can do.

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: The vote by Singapore was not only an enlightened one, it was fully in accordance with the rule of international law.

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: I ask this question because I noticed that both Myanmar and the Philippines abstained from the vote.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But having said that, I am not even sure that that would have been ideal.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, this was not an occasion to try to chorale or to put pressure on the individual members of ASEAN.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I say this in full cognisance that there will be, I am sure, future situations and future resolutions where it may be even harder for us to get together and to settle on a common position.
